Gene prediction and annotation of the most complete bins with Prokka. Commands for this step were run in `prokka/`.

# Find and annotate genes with prokka
Goal-  to use the BBD metagenome to improve our understanding of metabolic processes within the mat.Prokka will identify the gene sequences, it also uses a range of methods to identify homologous genes with known functions. If two genes share a common ancestor (ie are homologous) their functions are likely to be similar


# Metabat 2
```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka

cat ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt #run for single bin 
bin=metabat.2
prokka --cpus 2 --outdir $bin --prefix $bin  ../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa 
# --cpus 2: stops prokka from using more than two CPUs
```
**Cross reference results with those from checkm

```{bash}
#check output folder 
ls metabat.2
```

Run prokka on metagenome
Slurm script 
```{bash}
sbatch run_prokka.sh  #job xxx
squeue #check position in cue
tail -f slurm-551.out #track jobs

#check status
sacct -j 551 --format=JobID,State,MaxRSS,Elapsed
```

Enter bins into R (prokka)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
contig116 <- read_tsv("prokka/contig_116/contig_116.tsv")
metabat2 <- read_tsv("prokka/metabat.2/metabat.2.tsv")
metabat6 <- read_tsv("prokka/metabat.6/metabat.6.tsv")
metabat17 <- read_tsv("prokka/metabat.17/metabat.17.tsv")

```
